metadata.title: Matrix Reasoning: Rotation vs Reflection, with 5 Examples
metadata.description: Solve five original matrix exercises: track landmarks, tell turns from mirrors, separate movement, check symmetry and test operation order. Answers explained.

faq_items.question: How can I tell rotation from reflection in a matrix?
faq_items.answer: Specify the centre or mirror line, then track named landmarks. A rotation moves all points through the same angle; a reflection maps points across its line. Check more than one mark and verify a completed pair. Symmetric pictures may not distinguish the operations.

faq_items.question: Does a reflection always look different from a rotation?
faq_items.answer: No. A symmetric or insufficiently marked picture can have the same visible result under different operations. Exercise 4 gives a missing board that is predictable even though the operation is not uniquely identifiable.

faq_items.question: Should I rotate the whole matrix?
faq_items.answer: Only if the problem supports that relationship. Here each small board is transformed; the outer grid supplies examples and a missing board. Exercise 3 additionally moves the arrangement within its frame, which must be checked separately from its internal turn.

faq_items.question: Does the order of a turn and a mirror matter?
faq_items.answer: It can. A clockwise quarter-turn followed by a vertical reflection differs from the reversed order on the arrangements in Exercise 5. Check the stipulated centre, axis and completed examples rather than assuming all operations commute.
